question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at 8% per annum for 3 years is ₹360 more than the simple interest on the same sum at 6% per annum for 3 years. Find the principal.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate % for 3 years at 8% = 8 × 3 = 24%

Effective rate % for 3 years at 6% = 6 × 3 = 18%

Difference in effective rate % = 24% − 18% = 6%

According to the given condition, 6% of Principal = ₹360

⇒ Principal (100%) = (360 ÷ 6) × 100 = ₹6,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate 1 (R₁) = 8% per annum

Rate 2 (R₂) = 6% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹360

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 8% × 3 yrs = 24% of P
 
 
 6% × 3 yrs = 18% of P
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Diff = 6%
 (₹360)

 6% of P = ₹360 → P = ₹6000

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (P × 8 × 3) ÷ 100 = 24P ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P × 6 × 3) ÷ 100 = 18P ÷ 100

⇒ SI₁ − SI₂ = 360

⇒ (24P ÷ 100) − (18P ÷ 100) = 360

⇒ 6P ÷ 100 = 360

⇒ P = (360 × 100) ÷ 6

⇒ P = 60 × 100 = 6000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated only on the principal amount for the entire period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Effective Interest Rate

For simple interest, the effective percentage of principal over T years is simply R × T%. This makes comparisons between different rates directly proportional and much faster to calculate.

Difference Between SI and CI

For the first year (compounded annually), SI and CI are strictly equal. From the second year onwards, CI is always greater than SI because interest is continuously earned on the accumulated interest.
